extracted.intended_audience: British policymakers, statesmen, and educated public concerned with constitutional design (late-18th-century context)
extracted.subtask_description: Normative evaluation of revolutionary constitutional arrangements, providing standards for assessing executive power, ministers, judicature, military organization, and municipal authority in a new government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers must be chosen by affections/trust, not only by affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: These ministers, who were chosen by affairs, not by affections, acted in the name of, and in trust for, kings, and not as their avowed, constitutional, and ostensible masters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ministers owe their place only to transient circumstances (not to the sovereign's confidence), they cannot cordially infuse vigor into measures; lack of personal trust produces counteraction between sovereign and ministers. Anti-pattern: ministers installed by factions or assemblies who are in 'the highest degree ill affected' to the sovereign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers must have sovereign confidence and real discretion to serve effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: They are to execute, without power; they are to be responsible, without discretion; they are to deliberate, without choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibility without discretion yields poor service; ministers who lack confidence from sovereign or independence from assemblies will be passive/defensive and mutually counteracting with the nominal sovereign. Example: ministers forced upon a king will sympathize with him but lack capacity to execute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence and symmetry between supreme government and its executors
rubrics_metrics.description: I see nothing in the executive force (I cannot call it authority) that has even an appearance of vigor, or that has the smallest degree of just correspondence or symmetry, or amicable relation with the supreme power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional instruments must align the powers and duties of executive officers with the supreme authority; mismatch produces inefficiency and decay. Anti-pattern: a 'fictitious' executive apparatus costing much but performing little.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid maintaining dual real/fictitious establishments of government
rubrics_metrics.description: You have settled, by an economy as perverted as the policy, two establishments of government -- one real, one fictitious. Both maintained at a vast expense, but the fictitious at, I think, the greatest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not preserve ceremonial/pageant instruments that are expensive and useless; either make such instruments effective or dispense with them. Example: keeping a royal show without meaningful prerogatives is wasteful and destabilizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key prerogatives (esp. peace and war) should be entrusted appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: For instance, among many others, it was in your power to leave to your king the right of peace and war... There is no other way of keeping the several potentates of Europe from intriguing distinctly and personally with the members of your Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The right of peace and war is both dangerous and necessary; if not vested in a trusted sovereign, constitutions must design indirect correctives/controls to prevent foreign intrigue. Anti-pattern: diffusing this prerogative so foreign powers can influence internal actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers who cannot serve with authority should resign or not be retained
rubrics_metrics.description: I hear that the persons who are called ministers have signified an intention of resigning their places. I am rather astonished that they have not resigned long since.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministers placed in subordinate servitude, executing without power and answerable without discretion, cannot effectively serve; their continued tenure produces degradation of office. Example: ministers who are forced on a king or who are carried out by committees of the Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judiciary must be independent, permanent, and serve as a check on power
rubrics_metrics.description: They possessed one fundamental excellence: they were independent. The most doubtful circumstance attendant on their office, that of its being vendible, contributed however to this independence of character. They held for life... They composed permanent bodies politic, constituted to resist arbitrary innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent, life-tenured courts provide certainty, stability, protection of laws and private property, and act as balances against both monarchic and democratic excess. Anti-pattern: temporary, elective local judges vulnerable to faction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve remonstrance/registering powers as judicial checks on legislative decrees
rubrics_metrics.description: It would have been prudent, along with the parliaments, to preserve their ancient power of registering, and of remonstrating at least upon, all the decrees of the National Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing a judicial or quasi-judicial body to remonstrate and register decrees helps square occasional legislative decrees to general jurisprudence; prevents 'psephismata' (occasional decrees) that undermine legal consistency. Anti-pattern: vesting remonstrance in the executive who must execute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid governance by occasional decrees (psephismata) that break legal consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The vice of the ancient democracies... was that they ruled, as you do, by occasional decrees, psephismata. This practice soon broke in upon the tenor and consistency of the laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A legal system should favor stable, general laws over ad hoc decrees; otherwise public respect and consistency of law are eroded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges must not be subordinated to future Assembly orders that change rules mid-cause
rubrics_metrics.description: You first appoint judges, who, I suppose, are to determine according to law, and then you let them know that, at some time or other, you intend to give them some law by which they are to determine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Swearing judges to obey orders and instructions from a legislative body that may retrospectively change rules makes judicial discretion meaningless and dangerous. Anti-pattern: judges bound to legislative commands while being locally appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid temporary, elective, locally dependent judges (sexennial elective judicatories)
rubrics_metrics.description: In that constitution, elective temporary, local judges, such as you have contrived, exercising their dependent functions in a narrow society, must be the worst of all tribunals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elective local judges breed partiality, faction, and injustice toward strangers, minorities, and defeated parties. Use permanent, impartial tribunals instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative bodies should be subject to law and judicial coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative bodies are carefully exempted from the jurisdiction of these new tribunals... Those who execute public pecuniary trusts ought of all men to be the most strictly held to their duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exempting administrators from judicial review creates sovereign-like independent corporations and undermines accountability; administrative bodies must be coercible by law or be accountable in a manner that is not merely to a volatile assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: High state tribunal must be independent and not an instrument of the Assembly's inquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: This tribunal, subservient to their inquisition, the Committee of Research, will extinguish the last sparks of liberty in France and settle the most dreadful and arbitrary tyranny ever known... They must not evoke from or send to it the causes relative to their own members, at their pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supreme criminal/state court must not judge matters at the whim of the legislature or its investigative committees; avoid locating such a tribunal in the political heart (e.g., Paris) where it will be subservient and oppressive.

rubrics_metrics.name: The army must be an instrument under command, not a deliberative body
rubrics_metrics.description: The nature of things requires that the army should never act but as an instrument. The moment that, erecting itself into a deliberative body, it shall act according to its own resolutions, the government... will immediately degenerate into a military democracy -- a species of political monster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain strict military discipline and a clear chain of command; prevent the formation of soldier assemblies or comices that make military bodies independent political actors. Anti-pattern: troops holding committees, trying officers, or executing their own resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent irregular soldier committees and mutinous consultations that undermine command
rubrics_metrics.description: Those irregular consultations and turbulent committees formed in some regiments by the common soldiers and non-commissioned officers without the knowledge, or even in contempt of the authority, of their superiors...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such soldier-led assemblies negate legitimate military authority and encourage mutiny; measures must ensure officers' presence and authority are decisive, not bypassed by popular military cabals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oaths and proclamations alone are insufficient to restore discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: After the secretary at war had stated that the regiments had paid no regard to oaths... they propose -- what? More oaths. They renew decrees and proclamations as they experience their insufficiency, and they multiply oaths in proportion as they weaken in the minds of men, the sanctions of religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliance on repeated oaths/proclamations is ineffective when social lessons and incentives have undermined loyalty; practical institutional measures and authority are required rather than rhetorical/legal reiteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mixing soldiers into municipal clubs and feasts; it destroys military subordination
rubrics_metrics.description: The king has promulgated... that the several corps should join themselves with the clubs and confederations in the several municipalities, and mix with them in their feasts and civic entertainments!... It will make them admirable citizens after the French mode, but not quite so good soldiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civic fraternization with mutinous municipal societies will erode officers' primacy and convert soldiers into municipal partisans, increasing mutinous audacity. Anti-pattern: encouraging soldiers' social integration into politicized municipal clubs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Municipalities must not arrogate authority over troops or command them
rubrics_metrics.description: These municipalities arrogate to themselves an authority over the troops which your institutions have reserved wholly to the monarch... they break the officers, ... give orders to the soldiers, ... enslave the troops to the caprice of each of the cities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve clear civil-military boundaries: municipalities may requisition but must not command troops. Allowing municipalities to command troops invites fragmentation of national authority and local enslavement of military forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officer nomination and promotion must preserve clear seat of power and military chain of command
rubrics_metrics.description: You seem to have given the provisional nomination of the officers in the first instance to the king, with a reserve of approbation by the National Assembly... The officers must, therefore, look to their intrigues in that Assembly as the sole certain road to promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make officer appointment processes clear and avoid divided appointment power that incentivizes officers to seek promotion through assembly intrigue rather than command competence. Officers should act as commanders, not electioneering candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional parts must be coherent; avoid contradictory relations that breed anarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: What you may do finally does not appear, nor is it of much moment whilst the strange and contradictory relation between your army and all the parts of your republic, as well as the puzzled relation of those parts to each other and to the whole, remain as they are.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design institutions with mutual coherence and clear relations; piecemeal or inconsistent arrangements (executive vs assembly vs municipalities vs judiciary vs army) create systemic instability and recurring disorders.
